key_insight: HiPhy tackles a major gap in video generation: making videos not just look realistic, but behave plausibly under real-world physics. It introduces a hierarchical alignment strategy so multiple physical principles can be respected at once within the same generated scene.
problem_solved: Current video generation models often ignore or violate physics, especially when several physical principles must interact simultaneously, such as buoyancy, fluid motion, gravity, and object interaction in one video.
method: Uses hierarchical alignment to guide generation toward physically plausible behavior at multiple levels of abstraction.
Aligns generated video content with underlying physical principles so different forces and interactions remain coherent together.
Targets multi-principle scenarios where several physics rules must be satisfied simultaneously rather than independently.
impact: This matters for practitioners because physically plausible generation is essential for robotics, simulation, virtual worlds, and scientific content creation. It moves video models closer to being reliable world simulators instead of purely appearance-driven generators.
visual_elements: A split-screen comparison of realistic-looking but physically incorrect vs physically plausible generated videos
A layered diagram showing hierarchical alignment across scene, object, and motion levels
An icon-based physics map illustrating multiple principles like gravity, buoyancy, and fluid dynamics interacting together
A pipeline graphic showing input prompt -> hierarchical physical guidance -> generated video
paper_title: HiPhy: Hierarchical Alignment for Physically-Plausible Multi-Principle Video Generation
paper_authors: Tahira Kazimi, Shubhankar Borse, Munawar Hayat, Fatih Porikli, Pinar Yanardag
